title: Positive Range Add
objective: Structurally prove overflow safety for positive int64 range index plus one in authenticated checked private graphs while preserving checked fallbacks and hostile boundary behavior

oracles: checked private fallback and generated C differential

handoff.summary: Added a graph-authenticated theorem for `index + 1` and `1 + index` inside positive int64 ranges. The theorem consumes the existing nonnegative range-upper relation, preserves the tighter result interval `[1, INT64_MAX]`, propagates through copies and private calls, and retains checked public or structurally changed fallbacks. Focused tests cover direct-result emission, commuted operands, copied indices, near-INT64_MAX behavior, and stale, forged, partial, and mutated private graphs.
risks: This narrow theorem proves only a unit successor of an existing positive-range relation; it does not infer general affine loop invariants.

The broad `pnpm test:changed` run completed a converged production build and architecture checks, then stopped on the known unrelated `test/module-cache.cjs` `$rho$sigma$py$Any` failure also observed on adjacent lanes.
next_steps: Combine with the independently authenticated unit-range latch theorem and replay the frozen 7,081-output catalog before integration.
Measure generated checked-add counts, status-path collapse, ELF text, and paired timing against f285 before claiming a performance improvement.
